author: T. I. Dutton
title: Hanover Road and Townline Highway bridges reopen under MDOT bridge bundling program
text:
Hanover Road and Townline Highway bridges reopen under MDOT bridge bundling program
T. I. Dutton
The Hanover Road bridge in Jackson County and the Townline Highway bridge in Lenawee County were completed and reopened to traffic recently as part of the Michigan Department of Transportation's local agency bridge bundling program, according to a July 1 announcement. The bridges were included in phase three of a $9.8 million design-bid-build bundle within MDOT's University and Southwest regions.
The Hanover Road Bridge, closed since June 2019 due to buckling steel beams, reopened on May 27 after construction began in October 2025. The Townline Highway Bridge, which had been closed for years because of its critical condition, reopened on June 30 following work that started in November 2025. Charles Briner, director of engineering for the Jackson County Department of Transportation, said, “Reopening the Hanover Road Bridge restores an important link between two county primary roads, one that matters to commuters, area farmers and first responders. With it closed, emergency vehicles faced a 9-mile detour that added about 15 minutes to response times. Getting this bridge back open is a real benefit to the community.”
Briner also said, “The bridge bundling program has worked extremely well for Jackson County. As a local agency, a full bridge replacement is a heavy lift. The coordination among MDOT, the design consultant and the contractor was excellent, and we'd gladly take part again.”
Scott Merillat, managing director of the Lenawee County Road Commission, said: "The Townline Highway bridge was in critical condition and has been closed to traffic for years." He continued: "While it has been closed, we explored other funding sources; however, limited bridge funding meant this structure was never funded. Including this bridge in the bridge bundling pilot project allowed its replacement. We are thrilled that the bridge will open, as the detour in place has affected school bus routes, commuters, farmers and emergency vehicles for many years."
Bridge bundling packages several locations under one contract to streamline coordination and permitting while increasing economies of scale across Michigan’s local routes. In October 2024, MDOT received competitive federal grant funding on behalf of local agencies so additional bundles could be built; over five years this program delivered 38 replacements or removals statewide with no cost incurred by participating agencies.
MDOT manages nearly 10,000 miles of state highways—including M-, I-, US-routes—and more than 4,800 bridges while overseeing rail services, public transit, aviation programs, non-motorized trails, and safety standards across seven regions with over 2,800 employees, according to the official website.
